newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.Korean won ends lower despite BOK intervention.
newsitem.headline: S.Korean won ends lower despite BOK intervention.

text.p: The South Korean won ended lower against the U.S. unit on Tuesday, despite supportive dollar sales by the central Bank of Korea in the one-month forward trading market, traders said.
The won ended at 869.20 after opening at 868.90. It ranged from 868.50 to 870.00.
"Central bank intervention in forward trading temporarily boosted the won. But dollar short-covering emerged, pushing the domestic currency back down," said a local bank dealer.
Dealers said the central bank stepped into the forward market for the first time ever when the won fell to 874 against the dollar. It sold about $20 million, they said.
But the central bank denied intervening.
"The dollar's bullish trend isn't over yet," said a foreign bank dealer.
Dealers put Wednesday's trading range at between 869-870. The base mid-rate will be pegged at 869.30 against Tuesday's 867.80.
